chunks: And from him, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Kayshan, who said:

I wrote to Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who divorces his wife, and she demands the dowry from him. Our companions narrated that if he consummated the marriage with her, she is not entitled to a dow. So he (peace be upon him) wrote back: 'She is not entitled to a dowry.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He entered with her (consummated the marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife's dowry if she is divorced after consummation but before the marriage is fully finalized in some Shia interpretations?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the scholar clarifies a specific legal nuance regarding the dowry (mahr) when a husband divorces his wife after consummation (dakhala biha). Contrary to the common assumption that consummation guarantees the full dowry, the Imam rules 'la mahra laha' (no dowry for her), likely referring to the specific context of a *khula'* (redemption) divorce or a particular interpretation of the verse where the wife forfeits her right in exchange for release. This highlights the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between general marital rights and specific contractual conditions in divorce scenarios.
